newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals called to open mixed.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals called to open mixed.

text.p: COMEX and NYMEX precious metals futures were called to open mixed Wednesday, with gold and silver seen weaker but platinum and palladium higher.

Despite news Russian platinum group metal exports may resume June 20, after a five-month hiatus, platinum fixed at $425.00 an ounce in London Wednesday, its highest since Feb 7, 1996. Palladium fixed at $210, its highest since fixings began in 1989 and the highest spot market price since 1980.
Platinum lease rates rose to around 50 percent Wednesday for one month, up from 40 percent Tuesday, while one-month palladium lending rates soared to over 100 percent from around 75 percent Tuesday.

"Even though Russian exports are due to resume, with no Russian exports for five months, world inventories have been run down and there's something of an old-crop/new-crop effect going on, like in agricultural markets," one analyst said.
"The old crop has run out, pushing up spot prices, and the new crop hasn't arrived yet," he said.
NYMEX July platinum was called unchanged to up $1.00 after gaining $3.00 to $401.70 Tuesday, while NYMEX September palladium was called up $2.00 to $3.00 after gaining $5.35 to $169.65 yesterday.
COMEX August gold was called down $0.30 to $0.50 from Tuesday's close of $345.70.
In the bullion market, spot gold was quoted at $341.50/$342.00 against the London morning fix of $342.40 and the New York close Tuesday of $343.50/$344.00.
COMEX gold stocks rose 97,694 ounces Tuesday to 975,594 ounces, while COMEX silver stocks were up 236,211 ounces at 201,582,321 ounces.
COMEX July silver was called down 1.00 to 2.00 cents from the previous close of $4.728.
